title: A two-reaction counterexample to the gross-amplification affinity bound
abstract: Despons, De Decker and Lacoste (https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.02366, conjecture following Eq. (33)) proposed that the affinity at maximum production flux is bounded below by the logarithm of the gross amplification ratio in seed-dependent autocatalytic networks. A two-species reversible mass-action counterexample is given by X ⇌ Y with forward/reverse rates (3, 2) and 2Y ⇌ 2X + Y with rates (7, 6). On the positive Y-stationary set, the production current has its unique global maximum at (X, Y) = (1, 1). At this point the exponential of the overall affinity is 7/4, strictly below the gross amplification ratio 2. The network has positive rates, an invertible net stoichiometric matrix, unit production mode and a positive detailed-balance state. The formal theorem establishes the counterexample; the correspondence with the published conjecture is supplied by the witness’s stationary branch and reactant matrix, together with the source’s affinity and chemostat conventions.
